title: Customer decision narratives and trigger mapping for model substitution
creator: Priya Singh
description: Goal: develop a concise set of buyer-facing narratives and a trigger map that explain why and when enterprise customers switch inference providers or model variants. Deliver a prioritized set of substitution triggers (technical, commercial, regulatory) and corresponding mitigation levers Redwood can operationalize (fallback models, reserved capacity offers, contractual clauses, edge regions). Output will inform sales playbooks, procurement thresholds, and product rollout guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Completed 15 buyer interviews across NA and EU with recorded notes and short transcripts
A synthesized Decision Narrative deck (<=10 slides) that highlights 5 archetypal substitution stories
A Trigger Map artifact that ties observable telemetry/market signals to recommended product responses
Priority recommendation list of 3 operational levers with estimated implementation effort and expected impact on switch probability
tasks: Draft interview guide and scoring rubric (privacy-safe, consent captured)
Recruit interview targets (CS customers, trial accounts, 3rd-party procurement leads)
Run synthesis workshop with sales and Solutions Eng (2 hours)
Produce Decision Narrative deck and Trigger Map artifact in Confluence
Share recommendations with Eng/Console/Legal for implementation feasibility review
comments: 2025-01-13 Priya Singh: Kickoff complete. Draft interview guide posted in Confluence. Targeting NA fintech, EU healthcare, and APAC adtech customers.
2025-01-20 Ethan Ross: First 5 interviews scheduled. Noted recurring concern: 'silent latency spikes' during peak windows drive procurement legal scrutiny.
2025-01-28 Marco Delgado (Eng): Reviewed draft trigger map. Suggest adding a telemetry signal for KV cache hit-rate drop as an early warning. Requests sample query definitions.
2025-01-30 Aisha Kumar (Design): Reviewed decision narrative mockups; recommend visualizing substitution paths as swimlanes to show time->decision steps.
2025-02-02 Ethan Ross: Interim synthesis shared with Sales. Early theme: customers treat sudden price-per-token increases and regional outages as equivalent substitution triggers.

2025-02-04 Priya Singh: Added final interview summaries for 12 interviews. Two customers requested anonymized case studies for their procurement teams. Follow-up task created to coordinate legal review with compliance@redwood.com.
Review feedback: Sales asked for cost-of-switch estimates for three archetypes (SMB search app, enterprise RAG platform, regulated finance provider). Assigned to analytics for quick model.

Trade-offs discussed: aggressive automatic fallback to quantized variants reduces latency/cost but may degrade quality; recommended explicit canary + customer notification as default for enterprise tier.
notes: Next steps: finish remaining 3 interviews (APAC edge customers), finalize Trigger Map by 2025-02-07, and convene a cross-functional feasibility review on 2025-02-10. Risk: sampling bias towards high-visibility enterprise accounts; mitigation: include two mid-market customers in final interviews. Deliverable will feed into PM-771010 prioritization for reserved capacity features.
